newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Littlewoods hopes for quick sale.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Littlewoods hopes for quick sale.

text.p: Britain's largest private company Littlewoods said on Tuesday it has already had interest from potential buyers for its 135 town centre stores, which it hopes to sell by the summer if it can get the right price.
"We've had people sniffing around as it were over the last few months," chairman James Ross said in a telephone interview.
He said Littlewoods wanted to sell the stores, which employ 10,000 staff, as a going concern. Ross said food retailers might be among those interested in buying the shops.

"We think there are about half a dozen (retailers) who have the capability of paying a really interesting price," Ross said, but declined to give a figure. He said more than 70 of the 135 stores were freehold properties.
Ross said the group hoped to decide whether to proceed with a sale by the summer.
Many of the stores are in prime retail sites, and have a good geographic spread around the country. Ross said Littlewoods price and would continue to invest in the business.

The Moores family, which owns the group, has been dissatisfied with the company's recent performance and came close to selling the business in 1995. But Ross said that a sale of the entire group was not now on the agenda.

He said Littlewoods considered it was a good time to try and sell the stores. A booming retail market, rising rents and restriction on out of town developments could make the group's stores attractive to a number of buyers.
"There are a number of people hungry for extra space.....If they can do better of the square footage than we can you might just find...quite a lot of interest coming through."
